subject: Clarify: no-training opt-out, prompt/response ownership & subprocessor transfer plan
messages:
From: Clara Hunt <clara.hunt@novamed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@novamed.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data use commitments for pilot — no-training, ownership and subprocessor transfers

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare our procurement package I need a short, definitive set of answers for our legal and privacy teams so we can move to signature. Please confirm the following in writing: 

1) Can Redwood commit that NovaMed data provided during the pilot and subsequent production will not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any models (no-training / no-learn)? If yes, what operational controls and evidence (attestation/log exports) will you provide?

2) For outputs — prompt / response material — what ownership/usage rights does NovaMed retain? Do we get exclusive rights to outputs and any derivatives?

3) Please provide a current subprocessor inventory and tell us the plan/process if Redwood needs to add a subprocessor that will process our data. 

4) Cross-border transfer question: we need to understand options for EU residency and any onshore KMS options for keys.

Because of internal timelines, a short written response today or tomorrow would be ideal. Our procurement contact (Ben Rodgers) is copied.

Best,
Clara

Hi Clara — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary below; I wanted to loop in Jordan (legal) and Kim (privacy & operations) to confirm the specifics and attach the subprocessor inventory. More detailed redlines from legal will follow this afternoon.

Short answers (operationally actionable):

1) No-training / no-learn: Yes, we can offer a contractual no-training commitment for customer data under a pilot or scoped production environment. Operational controls we provide:
  - Dedicated customer tenancy and request routing that prevents customer prompts/outputs from entering model improvement pipelines.
  - A documented toggle and audit logs showing "learning" disabled for the tenant.
  - Monthly attestation PDF and exportable audit log (audit log includes timestamps, request IDs, model variants).

2) Output ownership: NovaMed retains rights to customer prompts and the generated outputs for your use. Redwood does not assert ownership over customer outputs in the proposed DPA language; standard derivative licensing is negotiable for special cases.

3) Subprocessors: attached is the current inventory (subprocessor_inventory_2026-05-14.xlsx). We have an approved process: customers are notified 30 days before onboarding new subprocessors with an ability to object for material security/privacy changes; for EU-residency sensitive subprocessors we offer an onshore routing option.

4) Cross-border / KMS: We can offer EU-hosted processing for data residency. For KMS, we offer: 1) Redwood-managed KMS hosted in EU region; or 2) customer-managed KMS (BYOK) with on-prem or partner-HSM options. Jordan and Kim — can you confirm the exact contract language and attach legal redlines?

I'll follow up with a consolidated DPA redline and a short operational runbook we can include in the SOW.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Fwd: DPA redlines and suggested clause language

Soojin / Kim — drafting notes for the DPA and SOW. Attaching the redline PDF (redlines_DPA_novamed_v1.pdf). Key items I recommend we commit to in writing:

- No-training commitment: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data for model training, fine-tuning, or model improvement purposes. Redwood will ensure data segregation and will maintain an auditable learning-toggle state for the duration of the Agreement."

- Attestation / evidence: quarterly attestation and a one-time audit export on request (CSV of request IDs and learning-toggle state). For pilots we can offer monthly attestations.

- Output ownership: include a clause: "Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in Customer Data and in Outputs. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, transferable, royalty-free license to Outputs for internal and commercial use." Avoid blanket exclusivity commitments for outputs that include Open Model-derived material; propose negotiated carveouts if they ask for exclusivity.

- Subprocessor additions: commit to 30-day notice and right to object for material changes; escalate disputes to mediation. Include a copy of the current inventory as an appendix.

- Data residency / KMS: offer BYOK with EU KMS residency clause and note that some managed features may be limited when BYOK is used.

Kim, can you sign off on the operational limits language? If OK, Soojin please share the redlines with the customer and include a DocuSign link.

Jordan Blake
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Data use commitments for pilot — no-training, ownership and subprocessor transfers

Hi Clara — Jordan and Kim reviewed and we've attached the DPA redlines and the subprocessor inventory. Summary and concrete commitments below for your legal team to review: 

1) No-training / No-learn: Redwood will add the following clause to the DPA: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, improve, or otherwise update any machine learning model, model weights, or model artifacts. Customer Data will be excluded from Redwood's model improvement processes for the duration of the Agreement." Operational evidence we will provide: monthly attestation (PDF), and an audit export (CSV) showing the learning-toggle state and request IDs.

2) Outputs & ownership: Redwood proposes the following: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Outputs. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to Outputs for any internal or commercial purpose." If NovaMed requires exclusivity over Outputs or derivatives, that would need a separate negotiated clause and potential commercial consideration.

3) Subprocessors: the attached inventory lists current subprocessors. We agree to 30 days' notice prior to onboarding any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data. For material additions, NovaMed will have the ability to object and request mitigation (onshore routing, contractual assurances).

4) Residency and KMS: options available — EU-hosted tenancy + Redwood-managed EU KMS, or BYOK with customer-managed keys and HSM options. There are some operational limitations with BYOK (e.g., certain telemetry features will be disabled); we've documented these in the attached "kms-residency-options.docx."

Next steps: I've attached the redline and the inventory. If this aligns with NovaMed's requirements we can prepare a DocuSign envelope for signature by next week. Ben — can you confirm purchase order template and timing?

Thanks,
Soojin

Attachments:
- redlines_DPA_novamed_v1.pdf
- subprocessor_inventory_2026-05-14.xlsx
- kms-residency-options.docx
